---

## The Problem (Why Upload Fails)

Payload's `type: 'upload'` field requires a **Payload media document** - meaning the image must go through Payload's upload pipeline (multipart/form-data POST, stored to R2 via Payload's storage adapter, a `media` row created in the DB with an `avatar_id` FK). Blogcraft passing a URL doesn't satisfy that - it has no way to create that DB relationship from just a URL string, which is why it never works.

---

## The Best Solution: Add an `avatarUrl` Text Field (Gravatar-style)

This is exactly what you described and it's the right answer. Add a plain text field alongside the existing `avatar` upload field. Blogcraft sets the URL, the frontend renders it. Zero complexity.

The change to `Authors.ts` is minimal:

Clean. Here's the full picture of what was done and what you need to do next:

---

## Summary

### Why the upload approach never worked

Payload's `avatar` field (`type: 'upload', relationTo: 'media'`) stores a **foreign key** (`avatar_id`) pointing to a row in the `media` table. Blogcraft can't satisfy that just by handing Payload a URL - it would need to fetch the binary, POST it as multipart to Payload's upload API, get back a media ID, and then set that ID on the author. That's why it silently fails.

### What was done

Three files changed:

1. **`src/collections/Authors.ts`** - Added `avatarUrl` text field alongside the existing `avatar` upload field. Both can coexist.

2. **`src/migrations/20260302_add_author_avatar_url.ts`** - Adds the `avatar_url` column to the `authors` DB table.

3. **`src/migrations/index.ts`** - Registered the migration.

### What you do next

**Run the migration** after deploying:
```bash
pnpm payload migrate
```

**In Blogcraft**, when creating/updating an author, instead of trying to push to the media upload endpoint, just set:
```json
{
  "avatarUrl": "https://your-r2-domain.com/path/to/author-image.jpg"
}
```

**In BlogCraft's frontend rendering**, use this priority logic for author images:

```typescript
// Prefer uploaded Payload media, fall back to avatarUrl (R2 URL)
const authorImageSrc =
  typeof author.avatar === 'object' && author.avatar?.url
    ? author.avatar.url
    : author.avatarUrl ?? null
```

### Can Payload "pull and import" from a URL?

Yes - Payload's local API lets you programmatically create media by fetching the binary yourself and calling `payload.create({ collection: 'media', data: {...}, file: { ... } })`. This would import the image fully into Payload's managed storage. But for your situation - where the images already live on your own R2 - **there's no reason to import them**. Using `avatarUrl` directly is simpler, faster, and keeps your image pipeline intact. This is exactly the Gravatar model and it works perfectly.

---

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

FORCE="${1:-}"

fail(){ echo "ERROR: $*" &gt;&amp;2; exit 1; }
warn(){ echo "WARN: $*" &gt;&amp;2; }
ok(){ echo "OK: $*"; }

[[ -f "CRITICAL.md" ]] || fail "Missing CRITICAL.md"
[[ -f ".xenco/meta.json" ]] || fail "Missing .xenco/meta.json"
[[ -d "scripts" ]] || fail "Missing scripts/"

DEPLOY_TYPE="$(python3 - &lt;&lt;'PY'
import json
d=json.load(open(".xenco/meta.json", "r", encoding="utf-8"))
print(d.get("deploy",{}).get("type","none"))
PY
)"

EXPECTED_ROOT="$(python3 - &lt;&lt;'PY'
import json
d=json.load(open(".xenco/meta.json", "r", encoding="utf-8"))
print(d.get("workspace",{}).get("expected_repo_root",""))
PY
)"

if [[ -n "${EXPECTED_ROOT}" ]]; then
  ACTUAL="$(pwd)"
  [[ "${ACTUAL}" == "${EXPECTED_ROOT}" ]] || fail "Wrong directory. expected_repo_root=${EXPECTED_ROOT} actual=${ACTUAL}"
fi

MANAGER="$(python3 - &lt;&lt;'PY'
import json
d=json.load(open(".xenco/meta.json", "r", encoding="utf-8"))
print(d.get("deploy",{}).get("manager_host",""))
PY
)"

if [[ -n "${MANAGER}" &amp;&amp; "${MANAGER}" == 192.168.* ]]; then
  fail "manager_host uses 192.168.x.x (invalid subnet for this cluster)"
fi

if [[ "${DEPLOY_TYPE}" != "none" ]]; then
  git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree &gt;/dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1 || fail "Deployable repo must be a git repo."
  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
  [[ "${ROOT}" == "$(pwd)" ]] || fail "Not at git root. cd to ${ROOT}"

  CHANGES="$(git status --porcelain)"
  if [[ -n "${CHANGES}" &amp;&amp; "${FORCE}" != "--force" ]]; then
    echo "${CHANGES}" &gt;&amp;2
    fail "Uncommitted changes found. Commit/stash first (or --force emergency only)."
  fi

  BRANCH="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"
  if [[ "${BRANCH}" != "main" &amp;&amp; "${FORCE}" != "--force" ]]; then
    fail "Not on main branch (${BRANCH})."
  fi

  git fetch origin main &gt;/dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1 || warn "Could not fetch origin/main"
fi

ok "Preflight passed."

```

version: '3.8'

# Payload CMS Stack for Docker Swarm
# 3 replicas with Traefik routing via traefik_proxy_v2 network
# Domain: publish.xencolabs.com
# Cert resolver: cf (Cloudflare)

services:
  payload:
    image: registry.xencolabs.com/payload-swarm:latest
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      HOSTNAME: "0.0.0.0"
      PORT: "3000"
      DATABASE_URI: ${DATABASE_URI}
      PAYLOAD_SECRET: ${PAYLOAD_SECRET}
      PAYLOAD_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL: https://publish.xencolabs.com
      NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYLOAD_URL: https://publish.xencolabs.com
      # R2 Storage
      R2_ACCOUNT_ID: ${R2_ACCOUNT_ID}
      R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID}
      R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}
      R2_BUCKET: ${R2_BUCKET}
      R2_ENDPOINT: ${R2_ENDPOINT}
      R2_PUBLIC_URL: ${R2_PUBLIC_URL}
      # Meilisearch
      MEILISEARCH_HOST: ${MEILISEARCH_HOST}
      MEILISEARCH_KEY: ${MEILISEARCH_KEY}
      # SEO Scorer
      SEO_SCORER_URL: ${SEO_SCORER_URL}
      SEO_SCORER_API_KEY: ${SEO_SCORER_API_KEY}
      SEO_SCORER_HEADER: X-API-Key
      # Image Gen
      IMAGE_GEN_API_URL: ${IMAGE_GEN_API_URL}
      IMAGE_GEN_API_KEY: ${IMAGE_GEN_API_KEY}
      # Support API Keys
      REINDEX_API_KEY: ${REINDEX_API_KEY}
      SUPPORT_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${SUPPORT_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL}
      SUPPORT_HEALTH_TOKEN: ${SUPPORT_HEALTH_TOKEN}
      PAYLOAD_ADMIN_API_KEY: ${PAYLOAD_ADMIN_API_KEY}
      SUPPORT_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED: "true"
      SUPPORT_TRIAGE_TOKEN: ${SUPPORT_TRIAGE_TOKEN}
      SUPPORT_AUTOFIX_TOKEN: ${SUPPORT_AUTOFIX_TOKEN}
      SUPPORT_ADMIN_TOKEN: ${SUPPORT_ADMIN_TOKEN}
      INTERNAL_LINKER_API_KEY: ${INTERNAL_LINKER_API_KEY}
      INTERNAL_LINKER_API_KEY_FILE: /run/secrets/internal_linker_api_key
      # Redis Caching Configuration
      # Native Redis VM Sentinel Cluster (not Docker) for HA session/auth
      # Sentinel nodes: xenco5 (10.8.8.17), xenco4 (10.8.8.16), xenco3 (10.8.8.15)
      REDIS_SENTINEL_HOSTS: 10.8.8.17:26379,10.8.8.16:26379,10.8.8.15:26379
      REDIS_SENTINEL_MASTER: mymaster
      REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD}
      # Dedicated local cache for query/page caching (Docker Redis)
      REDIS_CACHE_URL: redis://payload-redis-cache_payload-cache:6379
      REDIS_CACHE_TTL: "3600"
      # Enable caching
      CACHE_ENABLED: "true"
    networks:
      - traefik_proxy_v2
      - payload-internal
      - redis-sentinel
    secrets:
      - payload_secret
      - internal_linker_api_key
    deploy:
      replicas: 3
      placement:
        constraints:
          - node.role == worker
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '1'
          memory: 1G
        reservations:
          cpus: '0.25'
          memory: 256M
      update_config:
        parallelism: 1
        delay: 30s
        failure_action: rollback
        order: start-first
      rollback_config:
        parallelism: 1
        delay: 10s
      restart_policy:
        condition: any
        delay: 10s
        max_attempts: 5
        window: 120s
      labels:
        - "traefik.enable=true"
        - "traefik.docker.network=traefik_proxy_v2"
        # HTTP Router
        # Add all CMS domains here - separate with || for OR
        # All CMS domains - derived from sites_domains table
        - "traefik.http.routers.payload-swarm.rule=Host(&#96;publish.xencolabs.com&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.blogcraft.app&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.devmaestro.io&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.diabetescompass.com&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.fiberinsider.com&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.fightclubtech.com&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.fightmybank.com&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.homebeautyspa.com&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.imagecrafter.app&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.isthisagoodjob.com&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.landingcraft.app&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.landlordhell.com&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.lexiexplains.com&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.mcpforge.org&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.promptmarketer.app&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.resumecoach.me&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.snackabletiktok.com&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.sonomagrovesuites.com&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.tinatortoise.com&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.winecountrycorner.com&#96;) || Host(&#96;cms.xencolabs.com&#96;)"
        - "traefik.http.routers.payload-swarm.entrypoints=websecure"
        - "traefik.http.routers.payload-swarm.tls=true"
        - "traefik.http.routers.payload-swarm.tls.certresolver=cf"
        # Service
        - "traefik.http.services.payload-swarm.loadbalancer.server.port=3000"
        - "traefik.http.services.payload-swarm.loadbalancer.sticky.cookie=true"
        - "traefik.http.services.payload-swarm.loadbalancer.sticky.cookie.name=payload_swarm_sticky"
        - "traefik.http.services.payload-swarm.loadbalancer.sticky.cookie.httpOnly=true"
        - "traefik.http.services.payload-swarm.loadbalancer.sticky.cookie.secure=true"
        # Health check
        - "traefik.http.services.payload-swarm.loadbalancer.healthcheck.path=/"
        - "traefik.http.services.payload-swarm.loadbalancer.healthcheck.interval=30s"
        - "traefik.http.services.payload-swarm.loadbalancer.healthcheck.timeout=10s"

networks:
  traefik_proxy_v2:
    external: true
  payload-internal:
    external: true
    name: payload-postgres_payload-internal
  # Redis Sentinel network - provides HAProxy bridge fallback

    external: true
    name: redis-sentinel_redis-network

secrets:
  payload_secret:
    external: true
  internal_linker_api_key:
    external: true

```
version: '3.8'

# PostgreSQL Stack for Payload CMS
# Single replica with local persistent storage on manager node

services:
  postgres:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg17
    command:
      - "postgres"
      - "-c"
      - "wal_level=logical"
      - "-c"
      - "max_replication_slots=10"
      - "-c"
      - "max_wal_senders=10"
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: payload
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: payload
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    networks:
      - payload-internal
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
      placement:
        constraints:
          - node.role == manager
          - node.hostname == xenco3
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '2'
          memory: 2G
        reservations:
          cpus: '0.5'
          memory: 512M
      restart_policy:
        condition: on-failure
        delay: 5s
        max_attempts: 3
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U payload -d payload"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s

networks:
  payload-internal:
    driver: overlay
    attachable: true

volumes:
  postgres-data:
    driver: local

```

```
# To use this Dockerfile, you have to set &#96;output: 'standalone'&#96; in your next.config.mjs file.
# From https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/examples/with-docker/Dockerfile

FROM node:20-alpine AS base

# Install dependencies only when needed
FROM base AS deps
# Check https://github.com/nodejs/docker-node/tree/b4117f9333da4138b03a546ec926ef50a31506c3#nodealpine to understand why libc6-compat might be needed.
RUN apk add --no-cache libc6-compat
RUN corepack enable pnpm
WORKDIR /app

# Install dependencies - this project uses pnpm
COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./
RUN pnpm i --frozen-lockfile


# Rebuild the source code only when needed
FROM base AS builder
RUN corepack enable pnpm
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .

# Next.js collects completely anonymous telemetry data about general usage.
# Learn more here: https://nextjs.org/telemetry
# Uncomment the following line in case you want to disable telemetry during the build.
# ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

# Build-time only: Payload needs DATABASE_URI to generate types/importmap
# This is a dummy value - actual connection is provided at runtime via secrets
ENV DATABASE_URI="postgresql://build:build@localhost:5432/build"
RUN pnpm run build

# Production image, copy all the files and run next
FROM base AS runner
WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production
# Uncomment the following line in case you want to disable telemetry during runtime.
# ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs
RUN adduser --system --uid 1001 nextjs

# Remove this line if you do not have this folder
COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public

# Set the correct permission for prerender cache
RUN mkdir .next
RUN chown nextjs:nodejs .next

# Automatically leverage output traces to reduce image size
# https://nextjs.org/docs/advanced-features/output-file-tracing
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static

USER nextjs

EXPOSE 3000

ENV PORT=3000

# server.js is created by next build from the standalone output
# https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/api-reference/next-config-js/output
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

```

Everything is live. Now here are the exact changes you need to make in the Blogcraft backend:

---

## Blogcraft Backend Changes

### The Goal
When Blogcraft creates an author, instead of trying to upload the image through Payload's media endpoint (which doesn't work), just pass the R2 image URL as `avatarUrl`.

### Payload Author API Endpoint
```
PATCH https://cms.blogcraft.app/api/authors/{author_id}
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_PAYLOAD_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json
```

### When Creating a New Author
```json
{
  "name": "Jane Smith",
  "slug": "jane-smith",
  "bio": "Author bio here",
  "avatarUrl": "https://images.r2.xencolabs.com/your-bucket/authors/jane-smith.png",
  "site": 12
}
```

### When Updating an Existing Author's Image
```json
{
  "avatarUrl": "https://images.r2.xencolabs.com/your-bucket/authors/jane-smith.png"
}
```

### In Your Blogcraft Code (wherever authors are created/updated)

Find wherever you currently try to push to `media` or set `avatar`. Replace or supplement it with `avatarUrl`. The pattern in Make.com or your backend would be:

```javascript
// OLD (what you've been trying - doesn't work)
const formData = new FormData()
formData.append('file', imageBlob)
// POST to /api/media ... fails

// NEW (works immediately)
await fetch(`https://cms.blogcraft.app/api/authors/${authorId}`, {
  method: 'PATCH',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${PAYLOAD_API_KEY}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    avatarUrl: r2ImageUrl  // the URL you already have from image gen
  })
})
```

### In BlogCraft's Frontend (to render the image)

Use this priority logic wherever you render author images:

```typescript
function getAuthorImageSrc(author: Author): string | null {
  // Prefer the Payload-managed upload if it exists
  if (typeof author.avatar === 'object' && author.avatar?.url) {
    return author.avatar.url
  }
  // Fall back to the external R2 URL
  return author.avatarUrl ?? null
}

// Usage in JSX:
const src = getAuthorImageSrc(author)
{src && <img src={src} alt={author.name} />}
```

### In the Payload Admin UI
The `avatarUrl` field now shows up on the author edit screen with a description: *"External image URL (e.g. from R2/Blogcraft). Used when no uploaded avatar is set."* You can set it manually there too.
